details:
This is going to seem crazy but just bear with me.

I spent the past week trying to create a multiplayer game where players could fight AI enemies. But I found myself super frustrated because I couldn't use standard unity development techniques like interfaces to determine what could take damage, never mind using the heavily restricted udon APIs to communicate what took damage because the vrchat networking APIs are so basic.

I was inspired by the recent release of Vertigo 2.

And found myself super frustrated with the lack of APIs, and missing language features in udon sharp. I'm a senior developer in other contexts and I understand very well why udon exist from a security context. Things that just work in unity don't work for vrchat so you can't easily just port code to a vrchat world. 

For example lack of interfaces, lack of inheritance, extremely restricted networking capabilities. Never mind all of the advances that the unity engine makes in things like coroutines, or async functionality.

So the bar to create a world for VR chat Is artificially high because you're using these technologies that are not native to unity (udon).

Never mind the restricted networking API in udon. Which in and of itself deserves an entire feature request.

For a while I even wanted to build a world to visualize complex data from my work, but again this requires unrestricted networking access to restful APIs, and the full processing power of native c#.

My frustration is that unity is the super powerful game engine, and VR chat is trying to offer a way to expose some of that functionality without putting their players at risk, so the trade-off is a gimped world development environment.

But it occurred to me that VR chat could take a model much closer to how the app store works and arrive at a place that just sets it up for an amazing experience for users and opens it up to traditional game studios - by having a path which allows developers to leverage the full unity game engine to create worlds. Yes I'm talking full functionality like accessing external APIs or reading and writing files.

If developers can sign up for a certified developer program where the full unity API, along with native c# and the full VR chat API were exposed to developers, then they could create games that were much more engrossing and didn't require so much extra work to port. The challenge of course is that this then puts users at a greater security risk. Apple handles this by actually reviewing the API is utilized by apps published in their app store. Yes they're operating system has restrictions as well.

My feature request is that VR chat open up world development and allow full use of the native APIs in unity, along with their own APIs, and then require developers who want to publish these types of worlds publicly to be part of a certified developer program, and to submit their source code for review by vrchat, and perhaps charge a review fee.  Even if it was $200 to review one of these worlds it might be worth it, bad actors would be much less likely to bother trying to submit a malicious world if it costs so much to review.

Alternatively if you required source code to be submitted with these worlds and built a c# parser that scanned for usage of dangerous APIs and performed review around that API usage that would be an option as well.

Ideally developers could develop these worlds on their local machines without having to submit them for review. But upon wanting to publish them would have to go through a actual review process that validates the world does not put users at a security risk.

This feature request is driven out of my frustration with udon and u# and heavily restricted VRChat APIs.

The amount of development effort to bring udon/u# to parody with an unrestricted unity environment should be weighed carefully against this alternative. 

VR chat appropriately puts user security at the forefront, and I'm asking for a way to allow user experience to be put at the forefront by allowing much more powerful worlds to be developed, by changing the way we think about world development into a model closer to what Apple does for the app store.

Imagine how much easier it would be for game studios to bring their content to VR chat, for world creators to create much more engrossing experiences.
title: Unrestricted native unity worlds/with review process.
